key_insight: Token-level typicality relative to an expert model adds reliability signals beyond a generative model’s own confidence.
engineering_relevance: Combining expert-reference scores with standard confidence statistics could support detectors that flag potentially incorrect outputs across application domains.
method: Use an expert model’s token distribution as a reference, not as factual ground truth.
Train an AI ontology calibrator using student-model latent features and token-level output statistics to estimate expert-reference acceptance scores.
Aggregate calibrator scores with confidence, entropy, and perplexity into 15 response-level indicators for correctness classification.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on BF program generation, mathematical problem solving, and medical question answering show complementary reliability signals and cross-domain detector transfer, though transfer is not always symmetric.
watch_item: Agreement with an expert distribution does not establish factual correctness, and transfer performance may depend on the source and target domains.
paper_title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
